(This evening through Friday)...
Issued at 326 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

Rest of this afternoon and tonight...

Cyclonic flow around a broad upper low centered over the eastern 
Great Lakes combined with steep low level lapse rates will keep 
showers and gusty winds going for the remainder of the afternoon 
over eastern zones. Wind gusts and shower coverage has already 
diminished in western zones with isolated sprinkles expected to end 
by late afternoon. Shower activity and wind gusts are expected to 
diminish from the west across eastern zones into the early evening 
as warm advection in the 1-2 km layer overspreads the region 
diminishing low level lapse rates meanwhile the weak remnant 
deformation zone moves away from Indiana.  

Overnight, winds will continue to gradually diminish but won't 
become calm owing to a modest pressure gradient between high 
pressure over the Gulf and a deepening area of low pressure over the 
southern Canadian prairie provinces. Although skies will gradually 
clear from west to east through 06Z, increasing clouds later tonight 
associated with broad mid-upper WAA regime and a weak mid level 
shortwave combined with W-SW winds from 5-8 mph will keep min temps 
from falling as low as previously forecast and have adjusted temps a 
category up. There is some signal from the HRRR that some sprinkles 
may fall late tonight with thickening mid level clouds but given 
that this signal is faint at best, will leave out any mention of 
precip.

Saturday and Saturday night...

SW winds will increase during the day on Saturday ahead of a 
deepening upper trough and surface low pressure area over the 
Plains. With clearing skies in the morning combined with min temps 
around 32F most areas, have adjusted temps a few degrees warmer for 
Saturday. Skies initially be mostly clear Saturday evening before 
clouds increase from the west overnight associated with progressive 
system over the Plains. Increasing warm and moist advection out 
ahead of this system will lead to developing lower clouds and threat 
for showers to move in towards morning. 

Sunday and Sunday night...

Model guidance is fairly consistent in the timing and intensity of 
the seasonably shortwave and associated surface low moving through 
the region on Sunday. Recent RRFS forecasts have trended slower with 
the timing of the low/cold frontal passage late Sunday. A 30-40 kt 
low level jet will aid in advecting relatively high moisture for 
late November (PWAT near 1 inch). Model forecast soundings indicate 
very poor low level lapse rates will exist in the warm sector, but 
strong kinematic fields combined with weak instability (MUCAPE < 100 
J/KG) will lead to threat for isolated to widely scattered low top 
thunderstorms into early afternoon. Day 3 outlook shows best area 
for TS potential is south of I-70, and based on model soundings this 
seems reasonable. NBM initialized with no mention of TS, however 
have added to the forecast given the aforementioned reasons. Despite 
strong wind fields/deep layer shear, lack of stronger instability 
precludes any threat for severe storms. Nonetheless, strong forcing 
and high PWAT values will lead to another moderate rain event for 
central Indiana with most areas seeing totals between 0.5 and 1.0 
inch. 

The other concern for Sunday are the winds. Ahead of the surface low 
pressure area, S-SE winds will gust 20-30 mph, especially over 
eastern zones closer to the slightly better low level lapse rates. 
The biggest wind concern looks to be Sunday night. Fairly strong 
consensus exists on guidance showing a strong pressure gradient (10-
12 mb W-E across the state) in the wake of the surface low pressure 
and cold front. This combined with 40-50 kt low level jet from 1-2 
km AGL and steep low level lapses supported by moderately strong CAA 
along with deformation zone precip aiding in weak downdrafts all 
spells a recipe for gusts over 40 mph. Adding the NBM 90th 
percentile produced gusts around 35 mph, but sided with RRFS 
guidance which has gusts closer to 40 mph. Forecast trends will 
continue to be monitored for even strong winds if low flow better 
aligns with strongest pressure rises gradient. Lastly, guidance 
suggest that temps may briefly fall to less than 35 F for some wet 
snow to mix in (north of I-70 where thicknesses will be lower) 
before precip ends around 06Z. For now the timing, intensity and 
marginality of this snow all point to leaving out of the forecast. 

Monday through Wednesday...

In the wake of the shortwave trough, zonal mid-upper level flow will 
be prevalent early to mid next week. An area of high pressure over 
the Southern Plains on Monday will shift NE into the Ohio Valley by 
Tuesday. Although winds will not be calm Monday night, clear skies 
and relatively light winds point to the coldest night for central 
Indiana for the next 7 days with most areas seeing lows in the mid-
upper 20s. Winds should remain just high enough to preclude any
